newsitem.title: UK: IGC cuts world coarse grain crop, stocks due to US.
newsitem.headline: IGC cuts world coarse grain crop, stocks due to US.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) on Friday slashed its estimate for world coarse grain output in 1996 by 10.0 million tonnes to 866 million tonnes, mainly due a lower projection of U.S. maize.
But a crop of this size would still be a record and 69 million tonnes more than in 1995.
In its latest monthly report, the IGC lowered its forecast for world coarse grain stocks at the end of the 1996/97 season to 93 million tonnes, down 4.0 million tonnes from last month's estimate.
Projected output of U.S. maize was marked down to 225 million tonnes from last month's 232 million due to dry weather in the eastern corn belt.
Late plant development increased the risk of damage from autumn frosts, the IGC said.
Total U.S. coarse grain production was estimated at 254.6 million tonnes, down from last month's 262.2 million tonnes.
Coarse grain output in Russia, Kazakhstan and the Ukraine were also reduced by 3.5 million, 1.7 million and 1.6 million tonnes respectively following reports of lower yields.

But total output in the European Community was seen rising by 11 percent from last year, with the large portion of the rise coming from Spain -- now free from drought -- while the Chinese crop was developing well and the forecast was raised by 2.0 million tonnes to 124 million last month.

Central and eastern European crops were seen lower than last year due to unfavourable weather but latest forecasts were trimmed only slightly from last month. --Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
